newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Sept manufacturing output up 2.1 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Sept manufacturing output up 2.1 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Dutch seasonally adjusted manufacturing production fell 0.6 percent in September 1996 compared with August, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said.
September manufacturing production was 2.1 percent higher than in the same month of 1995, the CBS added.
DUTCH MANUFACTURING PRODUCTION Sept 96 Aug 96 Sept 95
NOTE - CBS calculates month-on-month changes on basis of seasonally adjusted index and year-on-year changes on basis of non-seasonally adjusted index.
Analysts had forecast a year-on-year rise of 3.8 percent for the September manufacturing figure and, month-on-month, they had expected a rise of of 0.8 percent instead of a fall.
The Central Bureau of Statistics said it had altered the production-indices from 1993 to bring the figures in line with the 1995 national account.
CBS said price changes and the amount of working days were among the factors that have been taken into account.
CBS said industrial output growth in the third quarter was somewhat lower than the second quarter.
During the second quarter output growth was 2.7 percent and growth was 2.0 percent in the third quarter.
Industrial output during the first nine months of 1996 was 2.0 percent higher, CBS said.
The base-metal industry saw output decreasing by 4.2 percent during the first nine months, while the overall metal industry showed the biggest increase with 3.6 percent.
CBS said the food and convenience industry, and paper and printing realised growth somewhat higher than average.
